topics.title: Trip to Mawlynnong: reading the details

learn.hook: Mawlynnong in Meghalaya is called one of the cleanest villages in Asia. Let's plan a school trip there!
points: A trip notice gives dates, times and costs. Read every detail carefully.
Use the costs in simple sums: cost for 3 children = 3 × cost for one.
To find how long a trip lasts, count the hours from the start time to the end time.
From 7 am to 12 noon is 5 hours; from 12 noon to 6 pm is 6 more hours. 5 + 6 = 11 hours.

example.q: The bus leaves at 7:00 am and returns at 6:00 pm. How long is the trip?

learn.reallife: Before any family trip, parents check the train time, ticket price and how long the journey takes.

items.text: Notice: trip on 14 March, bus 7:00 am to 6:00 pm, ₹250 per child, ₹400 per teacher. The trip is in the month of ___.

teach.nudge: What details does the notice give, and how do you find the trip length?

learn.hook: Oranges cost ₹60 per kg. How much for 2 kg? For 3 kg? Let's go shopping!
points: A price list 'per kg' tells the cost of 1 kg.
For 2 kg, double the cost of 1 kg: 2 × ₹60 = ₹120.
For 3 kg, add the cost three times or multiply: ₹60 + ₹60 + ₹60 = 3 × ₹60 = ₹180.
Doubling trick: double ₹45 = ₹40 + ₹40 + ₹5 + ₹5 = ₹90.

example.q: Ginger costs ₹120 per kg. How much for 3 kg?

learn.reallife: At a sabzi mandi, prices are written per kg on little boards. Shoppers quickly double or triple them in their heads.

quiz.q: Market price list (per kg): oranges ₹60, pineapple ₹45, ginger ₹120, tomatoes ₹38, potatoes ₹25. How much do 2 kg of oranges cost?
Market price list (per kg): oranges ₹60, pineapple ₹45, ginger ₹120, tomatoes ₹38, potatoes ₹25. How much do 2 kg of pineapple cost?

steps: So ₹45 per kg means each 1 kg costs ₹45.

steps: 3 kg at ₹60 per kg means ₹60 for each kilogram.

teach.praise: Double ₹45 is ₹90! Per kg means for each kilogram.
teach.nudge: What does 'per kg' mean, and what do you do for 2 kg?

revise.summary: A price 'per kg' tells the cost of 1 kg. For 2 kg, double it; for 3 kg, add it three times or multiply by 3.
focus: Find the cost of 2 kg and 3 kg from a price list
Double numbers using the doubling trick
Find the total cost of mixed items
remember: 'Per kg' means for each kilogram
traps: Don't add 2 to the price; double it
Don't double when 3 kg is asked
Don't double only the tens

topics.title: Shop bills: totals and exact amounts

learn.hook: Iba has exactly ₹163. Which items can she buy to spend every rupee?
points: To find a bill total, add the prices of all items.
To spend an exact amount, try combinations of prices that add up to it.
If a number in a bill is missing, find it by counting on: total − known prices.
A number line or play money helps: start at the known amount and jump to the total.

example.q: Prices: oranges ₹60, pineapple ₹45, tomatoes ₹38, sugar ₹20. Which four items together cost exactly ₹163?

learn.reallife: When you shop with a fixed amount of pocket money, you check different combinations to spend it well.

quiz.q: A bill has: rice ₹65, dal ₹48, oil ₹110. What is the total?
Prices: oranges ₹60, ginger ₹120, potatoes ₹25, tomatoes ₹38. Which items cost exactly ₹145?
steps: Add each pair: ginger + tomatoes = 120 + 38 = 158; oranges + potatoes = 60 + 25 = 85.

quiz.q: Prices: oranges ₹60, pineapple ₹45, tomatoes ₹38, sugar ₹20. Which combination costs exactly ₹163?
A bill says: soap ₹35, toothpaste ₹___, total ₹120. What is the missing price?
steps: Total = soap + toothpaste, so toothpaste = total − soap.
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of finding the missing part

quiz.q: A bill: biscuits ₹30, milk ₹54, bread ₹___. Total ₹124. What does the bread cost?
Iba has ₹100. Can she buy pineapple (₹45) and tomatoes (₹38) together?
steps: ₹83 is less than ₹100, so Yes, she can buy them.

quiz.q: Which pair costs exactly ₹100? Prices: ₹62, ₹38, ₹45, ₹65
A shop bill: 2 kg potatoes at ₹25 per kg and 1 kg onions at ₹40. What is the total?

teach.ask: Gappu has exactly ₹100 and wants to spend all of it on two items. How should Gappu choose?
teach.praise: I tried pairs until two prices added to exactly ₹100. ₹62 + ₹38!
teach.nudge: How do you test whether two prices make exactly ₹100?

revise.summary: To find a bill total, add the prices of all items. To find a missing price, take the known prices away from the total, or count on.
focus: Add a bill total
Find items that cost an exact amount
Find a missing price in a bill
remember: Missing price = total − known prices
Count on: start at the known amount and jump to the total
traps: Don't forget to carry
Don't add instead of finding the missing part
Don't forget one item or the 2 kg

learn.hook: You pay ₹200 for things costing ₹163. The shopkeeper hands back money. How much?
points: Choose notes and coins that cover the cost. Check: is the money enough?
Balance (change) = money paid − cost.
The same purchase gives different change for different amounts paid: with ₹500 the change is 500 − 163 = ₹337.
Count on to check change: 163 + 7 = 170, 170 + 30 = 200. Change = 37.

example.q: A bill is ₹145. Lou pays with a ₹500 note. What balance does he get?

learn.reallife: At a sweet shop, the shopkeeper says the change aloud as he counts it back. You can check it the same way!

games.title: Enough money?
items: ₹200 is enough for a bill of ₹185.
Two ₹50 notes are enough for a bill of ₹120.
Paying ₹500 for a ₹163 bill gives ₹337 change.
If you pay the exact amount, the change is ₹0.

₹200 is less than ₹240, so No, it is not enough.
quiz.mistake: Counts notes instead of their value

quiz.q: A toy costs ₹85. Raju pays ₹100. What change should he get?

quiz.explain: ₹200 + ₹100 = ₹300, enough for ₹275. The others are less than ₹275.
quiz.mistake: Picks an amount less than the cost

teach.nudge: How do you find change, and how can you check it?

learn.hook: Put 1 to 6 on a triangle so that every side adds to the same number. Can you make it 9? 12? 13?
points: A magic triangle has 3 corner circles and 3 middle circles. Each side has 2 corners and 1 middle.
Place 1 to 6 once each so each side adds to the same total.
Corners are counted on two sides. Small numbers at the corners give the smallest total (9). Big numbers at the corners give the biggest total (12).
Possible side totals are only 9, 10, 11 and 12.
13 is impossible: even with the biggest corners (4, 5, 6), the sides can only reach 12.

steps: Put the smallest numbers 1, 2, 3 at the corners.

learn.reallife: Puzzles like magic triangles and magic squares have been enjoyed in India for hundreds of years, even carved in temples!

games.title: Magic triangle facts
items: Big numbers at the corners give a big side total.
Corners are counted on two sides.
Each number from 1 to 6 is used once.

quiz.q: A side has corners 1 and 2. The side total is 9. What is the middle number?
Which side totals are possible in the 1 to 6 magic triangle?
quiz.explain: Smallest corners give 9 and biggest corners give 12. Totals in between can also be made.
steps: Smallest corners 1, 2, 3 give side total 9; biggest corners 4, 5, 6 give side total 12.
Totals in between, 10 and 11, can also be made.

quiz.q: To make the biggest side total, which numbers go at the corners?
quiz.explain: Corners count on two sides, so the biggest numbers there make the biggest total.
steps: Each corner number is counted on two sides.
So the biggest numbers at the corners make the biggest totals.
quiz.mistake: Puts the big numbers in the middles

quiz.q: Corners are 4, 5 and 6. The side with corners 4 and 6 must total 12. What is its middle number?
Why is a side total of 13 impossible?
options: Even with 4, 5, 6 at the corners, sides can only reach 12
quiz.explain: The biggest corners give 12 on each side, so 13 cannot be reached.
steps: The biggest side total comes from corners 4, 5, 6.
That arrangement gives 12 on each side.
So 13 cannot be reached. (Being odd is not the reason: 9 and 11 are odd.)
Answer: Even with 4, 5, 6 at the corners, sides can only reach 12

quiz.q: A side has corners 2 and 5. The side total is 10. What is the middle number?
What is the sum of all the numbers 1 to 6?
To get the smallest side total, where should 6 go?
quiz.explain: A middle number is counted once, so put the big 6 in a middle to keep totals small.
steps: A corner number counts on two sides; a middle number counts on only one.
To keep totals small, the big 6 should be counted only once.
So put 6 in a middle circle.

teach.ask: Gappu wants every side of the triangle to add to 12. Where should the big numbers go?
teach.praise: Big numbers at the corners, because each corner is on two sides! 12 on every side!
teach.nudge: Which circles are on two sides at once?

revise.summary: A magic triangle has 3 corner and 3 middle circles; place 1 to 6 so each side adds to the same total. Corners count on two sides, so the possible side totals are only 9, 10, 11 and 12.
focus: Find a middle number from the side total
Know which numbers go at the corners for the smallest and biggest totals
Explain why 13 is impossible
remember: Each side has 2 corners and 1 middle
Small corners (1, 2, 3) give 9; big corners (4, 5, 6) give 12
Possible side totals: 9, 10, 11, 12
traps: Don't put big numbers in the middles for the biggest total
Odd totals are not impossible; 13 is impossible because sides can only reach 12
Don't use a number twice

learn.hook: A village collected 1250 kg of plastic in March and 1475 kg in April. What a clean-up! How much in all?
points: Write the numbers one below the other: ones under ones, tens under tens, and so on.
Start adding from the ones place, then tens, hundreds and thousands.
If a place adds up to 10 or more, write the ones digit and carry 1 to the next place.
Check your answer by estimating: 1250 + 1475 is about 1300 + 1500 = 2800, so 2725 makes sense.
learn.reallife: Village panchayats add up the waste collected each month to see how clean the village is getting.

quiz.q: The village collected 1250 kg of plastic in March and 1475 kg in April. How much plastic is that altogether?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to carry from the tens place
Forgets the carry into the thousands place

quiz.mistake: Adds 2500 to 6000 instead of finding the difference

quiz.explain: 2000 + 2000 = 4000. We added 1 extra twice, so take away 2: 3998.
quiz.mistake: Rounds both numbers to 2000 and forgets to take back the extra

quiz.q: Three wards cleaned 1200 m, 350 m and 45 m of drains. How many metres in all?

quiz.q: About how much is 2980 + 4030? Choose the best estimate.
steps: Round each number to the nearest thousand: 2980 ≈ 3000, 4030 ≈ 4000.

Check by estimating
remember: Start adding from the ones place
Carry 1 when a place adds up to 10 or more

Don't forget to take back the extra after rounding both numbers up

learn.hook: 52 children and 6 teachers on the bus, 128 more joining at the next stop... How many in all?
points: Add 2- and 3-digit numbers in columns: ones under ones, tens under tens, hundreds under hundreds.
Carry 1 to the next place when a column adds to 10 or more.
'More than' often means add: '45 more than 238' is 238 + 45 = 283.
Picture data, like children learning singing or tabla, can be added to find totals.
Some sums need no carrying, like 324 + 152 = 476.

learn.hook: The village had 4500 trees. 1250 were planted this year. How many are old? Subtraction to the rescue!
points: Write the bigger number on top. Line up ones, tens, hundreds and thousands.
Start from the ones place. If the top digit is smaller, borrow 1 from the next place (it becomes 10 here).
With zeros, like 6000 - 2475, borrow across: 6000 becomes 5 thousands, 9 hundreds, 9 tens and 10 ones.
Check subtraction by adding: answer + number taken away = the starting number.

steps: Tens: 0 became 9 after borrowing from hundreds. 9 - 6 = 3.

learn.hook: A good problem-solver first asks: should I add or subtract? Let's learn the clue words!
points: Read the problem twice. Find what is given and what is asked.
Words like 'altogether', 'in all' and 'total' usually mean add.
Words like 'how many more', 'how many left' and 'difference' usually mean subtract.
Some problems have two steps. Do one step at a time.
Check if your answer makes sense.

revise.summary: Read a word problem twice to find what is given and what is asked. 'Altogether', 'in all' and 'total' usually mean add; 'how many more', 'how many left' and 'difference' usually mean subtract.
focus: Decide whether to add or subtract
Solve two-step problems one step at a time

On a train chart, add the people who get on and subtract the people who get off, station by station.
Total passengers who travelled = people at the start + everyone who got on later.

topics.title: Quick ways to add and subtract

learn.hook: 811 + 99 in your head? Add 100 and take away 1. Done in a second!
points: Near-round numbers are easy: + 99 is + 100 − 1. So 811 + 99 = 911 − 1 = 910.
Split a number to subtract in steps: 410 − 12 = 410 − 10 − 2 = 398.
Make a round number first: 326 + 25 = 325 + 25 + 1 = 350 + 1 = 351.
learn.reallife: Shopkeepers do quick sums in their heads all day: ₹99 is ₹100 minus ₹1!

steps: So add 100, then take away the extra 2.

revise.summary: Near-round numbers make sums quick: + 99 is + 100 − 1, and − 98 is − 100 + 2. You can also split a number or make a round number first.

learn.hook: 4☐7 + 25☐ = 703. Can you be a digit detective and find the missing digits?
points: In a number grid, neighbouring pairs can be compared: find the pair with the greatest sum or the smallest difference.
To find missing digits, work from the ones place and think about carries.
In 4☐7 + 25☐ = 703: 7 + ☐ ends in 3, so ☐ = 6 (13, carry 1). Then ☐ + 5 + 1 ends in 0, so ☐ = 4 (10, carry 1). Check hundreds: 4 + 2 + 1 = 7.
Many pairs of numbers can have the same sum or difference. Make up a story for your pair!

steps: Tens: ☐ + 4 must end in 2, so ☐ + 4 = 12 and we carry 1.

learn.reallife: Number puzzles in newspapers and magazines often ask you to find missing digits. Detectives use clues the same way!

quiz.q: Find the missing digit: 26☐ + 135 = 403.
quiz.explain: Ones: ☐ + 5 ends in 3, so ☐ + 5 = 13, ☐ = 8, carry 1. Tens: 6 + 3 + 1 = 10, carry 1. Hundreds: 2 + 1 + 1 = 4. ✓

quiz.q: Which story fits 'two numbers with a sum of 80'?
options: Ria has 50 stickers and Raj has 30; together they have 80
quiz.explain: 50 + 30 = 80 is a sum story about putting together.
steps: A sum story puts two amounts together.
Ria has 50 and Raj has 30: together 50 + 30 = 80.
The other stories are about taking away or groups of 10.
Answer: Ria has 50 stickers and Raj has 30; together they have 80
